takeaways: Changes of context happen only when the user asks for them, or there is a way to turn automatic changes off.
Level AAA. It goes further than 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, which only cover focus and input. This covers any change not requested, such as timed redirects, pop-up windows on load or automatic page refreshes.
Content that updates in place, like a live score, is not a change of context. Opening a new window or sending people to another page without asking is.
Sending people somewhere they did not choose can lose their place, their reading and their work.
failures: A “You will be redirected in 5 seconds” page
A pop-up window that opens when the page loads
A page that reloads itself every minute
check: List every change of page, window or focus in the flow. Mark which ones the user did not trigger.
For each one not triggered by the user, find the setting that turns it off, or change it to a button.
Check links that open a new window say so, so people can choose.

quiz.question: After people save their settings, the design shows a success page that sends them to the dashboard after 3 seconds. What meets 3.2.5?
options: Show the success message with a “Go to dashboard” button
Add a countdown so people know it is coming
quiz.why: A button lets people move when they choose. A longer delay or a countdown is still an automatic change they did not ask for.

spec: Mark every change of context and what triggers it.
Replace automatic redirects and refreshes with buttons, or design the setting that turns them off.
Note which links open a new window, with the visible or spoken label that says so.
review: Did the user ask for this to happen?
If it is automatic, where is the switch to turn it off?
What happens to someone halfway through reading when this fires?
tradeoff: Automatic redirects and auto-opening chats can lift short-term metrics. Full AAA compliance is worth aiming for in focused tools and forms; at minimum, remove timed redirects and auto-opening windows, which cost little to fix.
system: Remove auto-redirect and auto-open options from page templates and chat widgets in the library, or ship them off by default.
pitch: When we move people without asking, some of them get lost. Letting them choose when to go keeps them with us.
